newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China's SDB brings Yankee.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China's SDB brings Yankee.

text.p: State Development Bank of China's Yankee bond was the big deal in Asian debt markets on Thursday.
The US$330 million 7.375 percent notes due 2007 were priced to yield 80 basis points over 10-year U.S. Treasury notes. Lehman Brothers and J.P. Morgan Securities were lead managers.
The issue was increased between launch and pricing from US$300 million.
Some said the pricing was generous and sure to tighten.
"It's cheap and I wish I had some," said one trader who predicted that the bond will tighten a few basis points when it frees to trade.

"I think it was priced cheap to get it into the U.S," said another banker. "I think the borrower wanted to target U.S. investors and not have a good chunk of the issue go to Asian asset swappers. So it offered a slightly wider spread," he said.
State Development Bank debt is rated equally with the sovereign at A3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB by Standard and Poor's Corp.
China's global bond due July 2006 reportedly is trading in the mid 70s over the benchmark.
But Allen Cuttler, head of Asian debt capital markets at Lehman Brothers, pointed out that the SDB bond priced on the tighter side of the indicated 80-82 basis points range.
Moreover, he said, the China sovereign bond has been quoted out to 80 basis points "which puts SDP right on top of China."
Cuttler, who was speaking on Reuters Financial Television's weekly Asian Debt Briefing, said Lehman was pleased with the bond's pricing and by its size increase.
"This transaction, and the reception it has received, and what we expect will be a strong aftermarket performance, sets up a very nice stage for other Chinese borrowers lining up," he said.
China's sovereign bonds have performed extremely well over the last year. For example, the global due in July 2006 was priced to yield 110 over Treasuries at launch last July.

Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, and Agricultural Bank of China are contemplating international bond issues this year, a Chinese official said earlier this week.
Sixty percent of the State Development Bank bond placed in the U.S., with the remaining 40 percent roughly split between Europe and Asia, Cuttler said.

In other news, Germany's DSL Bank priced a 6.50 percent five-year Euro-Asian bond to yield 11 basis points over the benchmark. The bond is listed in Luxembourg, Hong Kong and Singapore. Merrill Lynch and Nomura were the leads.

Bankers said Hong Kong property developer Hysan Development has mandated J.P. Morgan to arrange its HK$2 billion floating rate note issue. The five-year notes are expected to pay an all-in return of 64 basis points.
Local bank Ka Wah is considering a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue, sources said.
There is talk that Salomon Brothers and Morgan Stanley may have picked up the mandate to lead the US$500 million global bond for Export-Import Bank of Korea (KEXIM).
Sources also said that Sri Lanka may be mulling a capital markets issue.
